newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's SARS says slow response to tax amnesty.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's SARS says slow response to tax amnesty.

text.p: South Africans have responded slowly to a tax amnesty intended to bring in over four billion rand in owed taxes, the South African Revenue Service (SARS) said on Tuesday.

The government granted an amnesty to encourage defaulting taxpayers to get their tax affairs in order before the end of February. Some 2.6 billion rand ($556 million) in penalties and interest would be written off under the scheme, SARS chief executive Piet Liebenberg said.

"We have received about a thousand applications. They are very few but (are) according to expectations due to the festive season...The amount involved is completely irrelevant, very minute," Liebenberg told reporters.
He said from March 1 the SARS would use the full force of the law to track down defaulters.
